_meta.source: Written for claudeDM (Sci-Fi category). Mostly original; a few general-mechanics sentences (e.g. opportunity attacks, passive checks, stat-block phrasing) are adapted from SRD 5.1, licensed CC BY 4.0 — see NOTICE.
_meta.notes: Sci-Fi weapons and armor. 'weapons' is a flat array; each weapon has a proficiency 'group', era tags, dice, damage type, range (normal/long in feet, or 'melee'), magazine size (null when not applicable), reload cost, fire modes, properties, cost and notes. Costs are in dollars for 1980s/modern weapons and in credits for future-only items; a credits campaign may price multi-era weapons at 1 cr = $1. Select-fire weapons in the Automatics group carry 'singleShotGroup': firing them in single mode uses that group's proficiency, burst or auto needs Automatics. 'extraDamage' is a second damage component added on a hit. Gunplay rules are in combat.json; general gear is in gear.json.

weapons.name: Knife
weapons.notes: Kitchen, folding, hunting or switchblade. Can be thrown 20/60 ft.

weapons.name: Combat knife
weapons.notes: Fixed-blade military knife, often worn on a vest.

weapons.name: Brass knuckles
weapons.notes: Replaces your unarmed strike damage if better; a Brawler adds +1 to unarmed damage instead.

weapons.name: Baseball bat
weapons.notes: Wood or aluminum. Two hands for a full swing.

weapons.name: Nightstick
weapons.notes: Police side-handle or straight baton.

weapons.name: Collapsible baton
weapons.notes: Extends with a flick; collapses to 8 inches.

weapons.name: Crowbar
weapons.notes: Also gives advantage on STR checks to force doors and crates.

weapons.name: Machete
weapons.notes: Brush blade; common in jungles, farms and zombie-infested suburbs.

weapons.name: Fire axe
weapons.notes: Also chops through a wooden door in 1 round.

weapons.name: Sledgehammer
weapons.notes: Breaching tool; deals double damage to doors, locks and walls.

weapons.name: Chainsaw
weapons.notes: Takes an action to start (DC 10 Mechanics in a hurry). Noise carries like gunfire. Runs 1 hour per tank.

weapons.name: Stun baton
weapons.notes: On a hit the target makes a DC 12 CON save or is stunned until the end of its next turn. 20 charges per battery.

weapons.name: Arc baton
weapons.notes: Hit deals 1d6 bludgeoning plus 1d6 lightning. Battery lasts 50 hits; recharge on a long rest.

weapons.name: Vibro-blade
weapons.notes: Ultrasonically vibrating edge; cuts through ballistic weave and hardshell plates.

weapons.name: 9mm pistol
weapons.notes: Standard semi-automatic service pistol (Beretta 92, Glock 17 and similar).

weapons.name: .38 revolver
weapons.notes: Six-shot police and civilian revolver. A revolver never jams on a natural 1; it just misses.

weapons.name: Snub-nose revolver
weapons.notes: Two-inch barrel .38; advantage on Sleight of Hand to hide it. Never jams.

weapons.name: Holdout pistol
weapons.notes: Tiny .380 or .25 pocket pistol; advantage on Sleight of Hand checks to conceal it from a pat-down.

weapons.name: Silenced .22 pistol
weapons.notes: Integrally suppressed .22; heard only within about 60 ft.

weapons.name: .45 pistol
weapons.notes: Heavy-frame single-stack pistol (M1911 pattern).

weapons.name: .357 magnum revolver
weapons.notes: Full-size magnum revolver. Never jams.

weapons.name: .44 magnum revolver
weapons.notes: Long-barreled hunting revolver. Never jams. A creature hit with STR 8 or lower or Small size must succeed on a DC 10 STR save or fall prone.

weapons.name: Heavy pistol (.50)
weapons.notes: Oversized semi-auto (Desert Eagle class).

weapons.name: Stun gun
weapons.notes: Fires barbed darts. On a hit the target makes a DC 13 CON save or is stunned until the end of its next turn. Robots and synthetics are immune to the stun.

weapons.name: Flare gun
weapons.notes: A hit sets flammable material alight. Fired upward it lights a 200-ft radius as bright light for 1 minute.

weapons.name: Caseless 10mm pistol
weapons.notes: Future service pistol firing caseless rounds; jams only on a natural 1 rolled twice in a row.

weapons.name: Flechette pistol
weapons.notes: Fires bundles of steel needles; quiet (heard within 120 ft). Needles are poor against hard armor: wearers of Medium, Heavy or Powered armor take half damage.

weapons.name: Pump shotgun
weapons.notes: 12-gauge buckshot. Scatter: +2 to hit within 30 ft, disadvantage at long range. Slugs instead: 2d6, range 50/150, no scatter.

weapons.name: Sawed-off shotgun
weapons.notes: Double-barrel, cut down. Both barrels at once: one attack spending 2 shells, +1d8 damage. Illegal in most places.

weapons.name: Combat shotgun (semi-auto)
weapons.notes: Tube-fed tactical shotgun.

weapons.name: .22 rifle
weapons.notes: Small-game rifle; heard within about 300 ft rather than for blocks.

weapons.name: Lever-action rifle
weapons.notes: .30-30 ranch and hunting rifle; reloading is one round at a time (an action loads all 7).

weapons.name: Semi-auto carbine
weapons.notes: Civilian semi-automatic rifle in an assault-rifle chassis; single shot only.

weapons.name: Battle rifle
weapons.notes: Full-power 7.62mm rifle (FAL / M14 pattern), semi-automatic.

weapons.name: Hunting rifle (bolt-action)
weapons.notes: Scoped bolt-action deer rifle.

weapons.name: Sniper rifle
weapons.notes: Military precision rifle with high-power optics; firing beyond 120 ft without Aiming first imposes disadvantage.

weapons.name: Anti-materiel rifle
weapons.notes: .50-caliber rifle; must be fired prone or braced (otherwise disadvantage). Deals double damage to vehicles and constructs' cover.

weapons.name: Crossbow
weapons.notes: Silent hunting crossbow; bolts are recoverable on a 50% chance. Cannot jam.

weapons.name: Machine pistol
weapons.notes: Compact automatic pistol (MAC-10, Skorpion pattern); can be fired one-handed.

weapons.name: SMG (Uzi pattern)
weapons.notes: Open-bolt 9mm submachine gun (Uzi pattern).

weapons.name: SMG (MP5 pattern)
weapons.notes: Roller-locked 9mm submachine gun used by police tactical teams (MP5 pattern).

weapons.name: Suppressed SMG
weapons.notes: Integrally suppressed 9mm SMG (MP5SD pattern); heard within about 60 ft.

weapons.name: Personal defense weapon
weapons.notes: Compact bullpup firing small high-velocity rounds designed to defeat soft armor (P90 class).

weapons.name: Assault rifle (AK pattern)
weapons.notes: 7.62mm Kalashnikov-pattern rifle; rugged, cheap and everywhere. Its rugged action means a jam is cleared as a bonus action instead of an action.

weapons.name: Assault rifle (M16 pattern)
weapons.notes: 5.56mm rifle (M16 / M4 family); lighter and more accurate than the AK pattern.

weapons.name: Automatic shotgun
weapons.notes: Drum-fed automatic 12-gauge. Scatter applies to single and burst shots.

weapons.name: Caseless pulse rifle
weapons.notes: Future infantry rifle with a digital round counter (you always know exactly how many rounds remain). Some models carry an underslung 40mm launcher (4 grenades).

weapons.name: Light machine gun
weapons.notes: Belt- or box-fed squad automatic weapon (M60, M249 pattern). Fired standing without a bipod or mount: disadvantage on burst attacks.

weapons.name: Grenade launcher
weapons.notes: 40mm break-action launcher (M79 pattern). Instead of an attack roll, choose a point in range: each creature within 10 ft of it makes a DC 13 DEX save, taking 3d6 piercing on a failure or half on a success. Can also fire smoke, gas or buckshot rounds.

weapons.name: Rocket launcher
weapons.notes: Shoulder-fired rocket (RPG / LAW pattern). Attack roll against a vehicle or structure; on a hit, double damage. Against creatures, choose a point: 10-ft radius, DC 15 DEX save, 6d6 fire, half on success. Backblast: anyone within 10 ft behind the shooter takes 2d6 fire. Disposable models cannot be reloaded.

weapons.name: Flamethrower
weapons.notes: Each use spends 10 seconds of fuel (1 'round' from a 10-round tank) and fills a 30-ft line 5 ft wide: each creature in it makes a DC 13 DEX save, taking 4d6 fire on a failure or half on a success, and catches fire on a failure (1d4 fire at the start of each turn until it uses an action to put it out). A hit on the tank (called shot, -5) detonates it: 6d6 fire in a 10-ft radius.

weapons.name: Plasma cannon
weapons.notes: Man-portable plasma projector. On a hit, every other creature within 5 ft of the target takes half the damage.

weapons.name: Minigun
weapons.notes: Rotary machine gun; normally vehicle-mounted. Carried requires STR 18 or powered armor. Takes a bonus action to spin up before firing. Full auto with it affects a 20-ft cube.

weapons.name: Laser pistol
weapons.notes: Magazine counts shots from a power cell. Silent apart from a crackle (heard within 60 ft). Smoke, gas or heavy rain imposes disadvantage.

weapons.name: Laser rifle
weapons.notes: Military laser; magazine is a 30-shot cell. Same smoke/rain penalty as the laser pistol. Never jams; on a natural 1 the cell overheats and the weapon can't fire until the end of your next turn.

weapons.name: Plasma pistol
weapons.notes: Short-ranged plasma sidearm; sets flammable material alight.

weapons.name: Plasma carbine
weapons.notes: Fires bolts of superheated plasma. On a natural 1 it vents heat, dealing 1d6 fire to the wielder instead of jamming.

weapons.name: Stun pistol
weapons.notes: Nonlethal: a creature reduced to 0 HP by it is stable and unconscious for 1 minute. Robots and synthetics take the damage as lethal.

weapons.name: Sonic disruptor
weapons.notes: Focused sound pulse. On a hit the target makes a DC 13 CON save or is deafened until the end of its next turn. Ignores half cover.

weapons.name: Rail rifle
weapons.notes: Electromagnetic slug thrower. Penetrates walls: treat full cover from any material short of an armored bulkhead as three-quarters cover.

weapons.name: Gauss carbine
weapons.notes: Coil-gun carbine firing ferrous needles; heard within 120 ft.

weapons.name: Frag grenade
weapons.notes: Choose a point in range: each creature within a 20-ft radius makes a DC 13 DEX save, taking 4d6 piercing on a failure or half on a success. Cover between the target and the blast adds to the save.

weapons.name: Flashbang
weapons.notes: Each creature within 15 ft of the point makes a DC 13 CON save or is blinded and deafened until the end of its next turn; on a failure it also takes 1d4 thunder. No damage on a success.

weapons.name: Molotov cocktail
weapons.notes: Shatters at a point: creatures within a 5-ft radius make a DC 12 DEX save, taking 2d6 fire on a failure or half on a success. The area burns for 1 minute; a creature that ends its turn in it or failed the save burns for 1d4 fire at the start of each of its turns until it uses an action to put the flames out.

weapons.name: Tear gas grenade
weapons.notes: Creates a 20-ft-radius cloud for 1 minute (heavily obscured). A creature that starts its turn in it makes a DC 13 CON save or takes 1d4 poison and is poisoned until it leaves the cloud plus 1 round. Gas masks grant immunity.

weapons.name: Dynamite
weapons.notes: Lit fuse (bonus action to light). Detonates at the start of your next turn or when thrown: 10-ft radius, DC 12 DEX save, 3d6 bludgeoning, half on success. Bundle of 4: 20-ft radius, 6d6.

weapons.name: Plastic explosive charge
weapons.notes: C4-type charge placed by hand (action, Mechanics DC 10 to set the detonator; failure by 5 sets it off early). Detonated by timer or remote: 20-ft radius, DC 15 DEX save, 6d6 bludgeoning, half on success. Breaches any door or wall short of a vault.

weapons.name: Directional mine
weapons.notes: Claymore-type mine placed by hand and triggered by tripwire or remote. Fires a 60-ft cone: DC 15 DEX save, 6d6 piercing, half on success. Spotting the tripwire: Perception DC 15.

weapons.name: Plasma grenade
weapons.notes: Sticks to whatever it hits. 15-ft radius, DC 14 DEX save, 5d6 fire, half on success. A creature it is thrown at directly (ranged attack) takes the full damage with no save if hit.

weapons.name: EMP grenade
weapons.notes: 20-ft radius. Robots, drones, turrets and synthetics make a DC 14 CON save, taking 4d6 lightning and being stunned until the end of their next turn on a failure (half and no stun on a success). Unshielded electronics in the area (radios, cameras, energy weapon cells) stop working for 1 minute. Living creatures are unaffected.

weapon_groups.Melee: Knives, bats, batons, machetes, axes and other hand weapons. Everyone is proficient.
weapon_groups.Sidearms: Pistols, revolvers, stun guns and flare guns. Exempt from the point-blank penalty.
weapon_groups.Longarms: Rifles, shotguns, carbines and crossbows, plus select-fire rifles fired single-shot.
weapon_groups.Automatics: Submachine guns, machine pistols and assault rifles fired on burst or full auto.
weapon_groups.Heavy Weapons: Machine guns, grenade and rocket launchers, flamethrowers, plasma cannons.
weapon_groups.Energy Weapons: Lasers, plasma, stun, sonic and electromagnetic weapons. Future era only.
weapon_groups.Explosives: Grenades, Molotovs, dynamite, charges and mines.

weapon_properties.armor-piercing: Against a target wearing Medium, Heavy or Powered armor, the armor's AC above 14 doesn't count (e.g. riot gear AC 17 counts as 14; powered armor AC 19 counts as 14). DEX, shield, cover and other bonuses still apply.
weapon_properties.concealable: Small enough to hide under a jacket or in a bag. Spotting it requires an active search or a Perception check against the carrier's Sleight of Hand.
weapon_properties.finesse: Use STR or DEX for attack and damage rolls (the same for both).
weapon_properties.heavy: Bulky or hard-kicking. Small creatures have disadvantage on attacks with it, and so does a wielder with STR below 13 if the weapon is a firearm.
weapon_properties.loud: Unsuppressed gunfire or blast: heard outdoors for about half a mile and throughout any building it is fired in. See combat.json noise.
weapon_properties.nonlethal: A creature reduced to 0 HP by this weapon is unconscious and stable rather than dying, unless the attacker chooses otherwise. Some nonlethal weapons impose a condition instead of or as well as damage (see notes).
weapon_properties.scatter: Fires a spread of shot. +2 to hit targets within 30 ft. At long range you have disadvantage and lose the +2.
weapon_properties.suppressed: Built-in or fitted suppressor. Heard only within about 60 ft and does not reveal the shooter's position to anyone farther away.
weapon_properties.thrown: Can be thrown to make a ranged attack (or to target a point, for grenades) using the listed range and STR or DEX.
weapon_properties.two-handed: Requires two hands to fire or swing. Firing a two-handed firearm one-handed imposes disadvantage.

light.name: Leather jacket
light.notes: Motorcycle or bomber jacket. Looks like ordinary clothing.

light.name: Aramid vest (concealable)
light.notes: Soft body armor worn under a shirt. Noticing it requires Perception DC 15.

light.name: Armored coat
light.notes: Long coat with aramid panels; also gives advantage on Sleight of Hand checks to conceal a Longarm with the concealable property.

light.name: Ballistic weave
light.notes: Smart-fiber bodysuit or clothing liner; indistinguishable from normal clothes.

medium.name: Flak jacket
medium.notes: Military fragmentation vest; also grants +1 to DEX saves against explosives.

medium.name: Tactical vest
medium.notes: Ballistic vest with trauma plates and magazine pouches.

medium.name: Plate carrier
medium.notes: Ceramic rifle plates front and back with a ballistic helmet.

medium.name: Hardshell
medium.notes: Molded composite armor shell over a pressure-capable undersuit; with a helmet it is a 1-hour emergency vacuum suit.

heavy.name: Riot gear
heavy.notes: Full-body police riot armor with helmet and visor. Grants advantage on saves against tear gas when the visor is sealed with a gas mask.

heavy.name: Bomb suit
heavy.notes: Explosive ordnance disposal suit. Speed reduced by 10 ft; disadvantage on DEX checks; resistance to damage from Explosives.

heavy.name: Assault armor
heavy.notes: Full infantry combat armor with sealed helmet, rebreather and HUD.

powered.name: Powered armor
powered.notes: Strength counts as 18 while worn (if yours is lower). Sealed environment (vacuum, gas, radiation) for 8 hours. Requires Powered armor proficiency; without it, speed 10 ft and disadvantage on all attacks and DEX checks. Power cell lasts 24 hours of activity.

powered.name: Industrial exo-frame
powered.notes: Open-frame cargo loader. Strength counts as 20 for lifting and grappling and its fists deal 2d6 bludgeoning, but it gives no protection from vacuum and the pilot can be targeted with a called shot (-2 instead of -5).

shields.name: Riot shield
shields.notes: Transparent polycarbonate shield. You can fire a Sidearm while using it; other firearms need two hands.

shields.name: Ballistic shield
shields.notes: Rifle-rated shield with a viewport. Only Sidearms can be fired while holding it. As an action you can plant it to give yourself and one adjacent ally half cover.

powered_armor.don: 1 minute (the suit opens and seals itself)

currency.note: There are no gold pieces. Each campaign declares its currency in campaign.json. Money on a character sheet is a single equipment line written exactly as shown in 'sheet_format'.
